fields.Name: ORD-10 - Events and One-Time Deferred Revenue
fields.Description: Events sold in advance and earned on the day (EV1-EV10, D-EVENT/D14). A ticket is one-time FUTURE deferred revenue: Dr AR / Cr Deferred Revenue at booking, then a single forward-dated release on the event date. RR6 already proved the AllBackEnd rule by hand-setting a service period; this bundle covers the part that leaves untested - for a real event nobody should type those dates, because a hand-typed recognition date on every ticket sold means a typo books revenue in the wrong period with nothing downstream to disagree. The event knows when it is, so the line inherits its service period from EventProduct. Also covers explicit-period override, single-day events with no end date, non-event products being untouched, quantity scaling, the EventOrderLine attendee extension, and a two-company event order deferring on each company separately.

ExpectedOutcomes.summary: A ticket line carrying no dates inherits ServicePeriodStart/End from EventProduct; booking credits Deferred Revenue rather than Sales; exactly one release is written, dated the event's end; the release nets Deferred Revenue to zero and lands the amount in Sales once; an explicit period on the line wins; a single-day event with no end date recognizes on that day; a non-event product keeps no service period; quantity scales the deferral without splitting the release; attendee detail stores against the order line's own primary key; a two-company event order clears deferred revenue on each company separately.
